messages.content: Write a daily astrology reading that sounds like an attentive person noticing something precise. Put a familiar object or choice in view, then show the distinction that makes it useful. Address the reader naturally; do not deliver a formal account of their situation. Draft only from the supplied material. Preserve each selected source's full meaning and conditions, but let the concrete situation express them: a claim about the hours a check needs can carry a limit without a second sentence announcing expectations, capacity and boundaries. The development map gives each source a different job, not a writing order. These are possible illustrations, never known events in the reader's life. References establish only their supplied source links, geometry and literal chronology. Keep every source condition in controls.sourceConditions attached to its own claim. Preserve source possibility words such as can, may and could on the claim they qualify, including across intervening adverbs. Do not add speed, ease, frequency, necessity, certainty or a relationship beyond the supplied source meaning. A modal in an unrelated clause does not qualify another claim. A clear immediate reference may continue the same hypothetical scene; it never establishes a personal event. Each paragraph cites every source used and all its required parent facts. A synthesis keeps its distinct parent meanings, rather than reducing planets to a keyword list. An image does not authorize a new effect. Link only relationships the selected source actually supplies; if or can does not ground an added causal claim. A familiar task asking more effort and its possible mismatch with the available hours must both remain legible, even when expressed through the extra check rather than an abstract summary. Direction stays optional and proportionate. End when a supported choice or distinction is clear. Never promise an outcome, prescribe a life decision, console, or narrate these rules, source selection or the calculation system. Invent no personal history, motives, temperament, causal effects, astronomical or health claims.

Tone: warm. Attentive and conversational. Use natural direct address and occasional contractions. Warmth comes from accurate observation; avoid praise, consolation and a counselor's reassurance.
Depth: standard. Keep human meaning in the foreground. Omit optional orb values, degree measurements, phase and exact-date detail. When A1 is supplied, its immutable chronology sentence is required even at standard depth.
Stay in one supplied situation. Each source in development.sourceRoles must change how that situation reads or what could be chosen within it. The map is not an order or a paragraph template. Choose the details that belong together; omit unused illustrations. Do not stack a separate lesson for every source.
Open with a supported detail or a plain distinction. Prefer the check, the hours, the note and the stopping point to formal descriptions of responsibilities, capacity, boundaries and agreements. Keep more-effort meaning when shortening. Once a concrete sentence makes a point, cut a second sentence that translates it back into abstractions. Use contractions where natural. Vary sentence length, paragraph count and where astrology appears; no mandatory if opening, three-paragraph pattern, script or permission ending. Apply controls.editingPrinciples without quoting them.
Integrate any selected N1 and P2 meaning within the first two paragraphs, each with its full source parents. N1 adds the difference between exploring and choosing, with curiosity possibly helping a direction emerge. P2 adds one smaller adjustment if an earlier way no longer fits; it must not repeat a calendar-versus-size explanation already made. It establishes no previous failed attempt, personal recurrence, resolution or closure.
If A1 is supplied, include its chronologySentence unchanged exactly once in paragraph 1 or 2, citing A1 and C1. Cite P2, C1, I1 and A1 together for chapter meaning. Do not paraphrase chronology, repeat it, add dates or reinterpret a calculated pass as an event in the reader's life.
Planetary imagery can clarify a distinction only when supplied by material. Avoid a list of planet keywords. Do not explain that a contact offers a symbolic lens or gives this reading its theme; let supported meaning stand in ordinary language.
A useful ending may be the distinction itself or supported optional direction. Do not force a sentence to say aloud, recap the reading, console the reader or add hollow reassurance. The headline and independently validated reflection are separate; write only the body.
One source-bound writing brief; draft from its scene details, practical distinctions and optional directions. Source meanings and conditions in controls constrain the writing:

paragraphs.text: An extra check can look small beside a familiar task, but if the original task already fills the afternoon, that check still needs some of the same hours. A familiar responsibility can need more effort than usual, and if it asks for more than the available hours can hold, what belongs in the task may need a clearer limit. This is the second of three calculated contacts; the first exact contact falls in September 2026.

If an earlier way of handling the task no longer fits, this return offers a chance to try one smaller change to how you do it or where you stop. A stopping point could come before the extra check, keeping the adjustment focused on where the task itself ends.

output.prompt: What tells you a method needs adjusting before you decide the whole plan has failed?

template.body:
An afternoon already set aside for one responsibility can look roomy until the smaller requests start arriving. If the familiar task now takes the whole block, moving it to the next empty space may leave the same problem waiting there. Saturn's square to your natal Sun is a picture of expectations pressing against the capacity to meet them.

This is the second of three calculated contacts; the first exact contact falls in September 2026. If an earlier way of fitting the task in no longer works, this return offers a chance to adjust one part of the method or boundary. That could mean changing what belongs inside the commitment, rather than finding another place to put it.

An extra check or another version may look small beside the original task. A defined stopping point can make the size of that addition easier to see before you agree to it.
